LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.label: HB 410 two-in-five field rotation cap
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.basis: HB 410 limits temporary full-season leasing off a single field to no more than two years in five. The lease-to-own instrument buys the water right, not the land, so the farm can keep rotating fields and the model does not need a repeal or a 2.5-acre enrollment multiplier.

LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.label: Water right acquired separately from land
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.basis: Utah allows water rights to be owned and transferred separately from the land where they have been used, and a change in place, nature, source, or portion of use goes through the State Engineer. The model assumes partial agricultural rights can be acquired and dedicated without buying the farm land; each transaction still has to survive that administrative process.

LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.label: Basin-wide curtailment authority for the lake
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.group: What the legislature would have to pass
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.basis: Prior appropriation administration protects senior water rights; the Great Salt Lake does not hold a senior right large enough to order basin-wide cuts at these volumes. The mandate assumes a statutory depletion limit, or an equivalent dedicated lake right, administered across the Bear, Weber, and Jordan basins.

LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.label: A charge on water consumed, not diverted
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.group: What the legislature would have to pass
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.basis: The scarcity charge and crop levy are modelled on depletion or over-application, not headline diversion. That requires statutory authority to charge consumed water and enough measurement to administer it.

LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.label: Protection for saved and leased water in transit
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.group: What the legislature would have to pass
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.basis: The model treats monitoring as increasing the amount of saved, leased, or acquired water that can be legally shepherded to the lake. The State Engineer materials identify that transit protection as a gap rather than a finished system.

LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.label: State-held lake water insulated from growth
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.group: What the legislature would have to pass
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.basis: The protected floor assumes water rights held for the lake cannot later be re-diverted to satisfy municipal and industrial growth. Without that statutory insulation, the model overstates the durability of state-held water.

LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.label: Compulsory acquisition from unwilling sellers
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.group: What the legislature would have to pass
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.appliesWhen: Only when repossession is switched on.
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.basis: Repossession is a modelled backstop after willing sellers run out. It assumes a condemnation-like power to acquire water rights at value and process them quickly enough to matter.

LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.label: Statewide residential limits with civil penalties
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.group: What the legislature would have to pass
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.basis: The lawn module assumes a statewide outdoor-watering limit, citation authority, collection, and dedication of the saved water. Today those pieces are local and partial rather than one basin-wide lake instrument.

LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.label: Charges that switch off and back on at lake elevation
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.group: What the legislature would have to pass
LEGAL_ASSUMPTIONS.basis: The charge and mandate are controlled by whether they are still needed to hold the healthy floor, not by a permanent tax schedule. An automatic sunset and restart tied to lake conditions would have to be written into statute.
